# module homomorphism　`def.module-hom`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.module-hom)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.module-hom.md)

The set of all $A$-module homomorphisms is denoted $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M, N)$; under pointwise addition it is an abelian group. The kernel $\ker f$ and the image $\operatorname{im} f$ are both submodules; the map $f$ is an isomorphism $\iff$ it is bijective.

## Notes · **draft**
⭐ Examples: for $A = \mathbb{Z}$, module homomorphisms are abelian group homomorphisms; for $A = K$, they are linear maps.

⚠ In general $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M, N)$ is only an abelian group, not an $A$-module; a natural $A$-module structure exists only when $A$ is commutative.
